beats.beat: The company operates through two verticals: retail (company-owned stores) and distribution (supplying to multi-brand outlets).
Revenue is largely from footwear sales. The filing states 'majority of our revenue from operations is derived from the sale of footwear' and is concentrated in the northern region of India.

A significant portion of revenue comes from Skechers stores. The company's relationship with Skechers is governed by non-exclusive agreements, meaning the brand may appoint other partners or go direct-to-consumer.

The company also has subsidiaries: Gaurik Lifestyle Private Limited (for Guess stores) and Nuvora Retail Private Limited (for Bugatti stores). Part of the IPO proceeds will go into these subsidiaries.
All stores are on leased premises; the company does not own any real estate. This creates renewal risk.

beats.beat: Revenue: ₹579.78 million (FY23), ₹1,720.05 million (FY24), ₹2,204.03 million (FY25), ₹2,025.86 million (nine months ended December 2025). The nine-month figure annualizes to ~₹2,700 million, indicating continued growth.
Profit after tax: ₹3.48 million (FY23), ₹34.86 million (FY24), ₹122.63 million (FY25), ₹173.25 million (nine months ended December 2025).
EBITDA: ₹123.33 million (FY23), ₹443.99 million (FY24), ₹570.71 million (FY25), ₹529.46 million (nine months ended December 2025). EBITDA margin improved from 21.27% to 26.14% over the same periods.

Operating cash flow: negative ₹54.99 million (FY23), positive ₹159.33 million (FY24), ₹340.21 million (FY25), ₹116.87 million (nine months ended December 2025). The filing notes past negative cash flows as a risk.
Total assets grew from ₹870.83 million (FY23) to ₹3,664.52 million (as at December 2025). Equity attributable to owners stood at ₹776.20 million as at December 2025.

Governance flags include: the statutory auditor of subsidiary Gaurik South Private Limited is not cooperating; some incorrect ROC filings and non-compliances with the Companies Act; delays in payment of statutory dues; CSR shortfalls transferred to PMNRF; and related-party transactions that may not be at arm's length.
Certain immediate relatives of promoters have refused to provide consents for disclosures required by SEBI ICDR Regulations.
Outstanding legal proceedings involving the company, directors, and subsidiaries are disclosed.

beats.beat: India's overall retail market was estimated at ₹112 trillion by fiscal 2026. The domestic apparel and footwear industry is projected to reach ₹7,300-8,100 billion by FY30, growing at a CAGR of 6.5-8.5% between FY25 and FY30.
Within this, the domestic footwear retail industry is forecast to reach ₹1,900-2,100 billion by FY30.
Key growth drivers include rising disposable incomes, e-commerce penetration, social media influence, and a growing working-age population.
The market is fragmented with local, national, and multinational players. Global brands like Nike, Adidas, Puma, Skechers compete intensely, leading to price wars and thinning margins.
Headwinds include counterfeiting, geopolitical tensions, sustainability pressures, and increased competition from new entrants as e-commerce lowers barriers to entry.

India's macroeconomic backdrop supports consumption: the economy is projected to expand 6.5% in 2026, urban population is expected to reach 567.7 million by 2030, and real GDP grew at a CAGR of 7.3% between FY23 and FY26.

beats.beat: Gaurik Fashions is a multi-brand retail chain that sells footwear and apparel under licensed brands including Skechers, Guess, and Bugatti through stores in northern India.

The IPO consists of a fresh issue of up to 62,00,000 equity shares (face value ₹10 each, amount not disclosed) and an offer for sale of up to 8,00,000 equity shares by an investor selling shareholder.

beats.beat: Fresh issue: up to 62,00,000 equity shares of face value ₹10 each. The amount is not disclosed in the DRHP (redacted as [●]).
Offer for sale: up to 8,00,000 equity shares by an investor selling shareholder. Amount also not disclosed.

The net proceeds from the fresh issue will be used for: (i) setting up new Skechers stores; (ii) investment in Gaurik Lifestyle Private Limited for new Guess stores; (iii) investment in Nuvora Retail Private Limited for new Bugatti stores and inventory; (iv) repayment of certain borrowings; (v) repayment of borrowings of subsidiaries; and (vi) general corporate purposes.

beats.beat: Heavy reliance on the Skechers brand: a significant but undisclosed portion of revenue comes from Skechers stores; any adverse change in that relationship could severely hurt the business.
Geographic concentration: a significant portion of revenue is derived from northern India; regional economic or competitive shocks would disproportionately impact results.
The company's retail agreements are non-exclusive; brand owners can appoint other partners or switch to direct-to-consumer models, which could erode market share.
The statutory auditor of a subsidiary (Gaurik South Private Limited) is not cooperating, which may impair financial reporting and compliance.

Negative cash flows in the past (FY23) and significant debt on the balance sheet (total assets ₹3,664 million vs equity ₹776 million) indicate reliance on borrowings; the company plans to use IPO proceeds to repay debt, suggesting leveraged operations.
